_comment: Single source of truth for the PL control-register map over PS GP0.
Edit THIS file, then run `make -C tools regmap` (or tools/gen_regmap.py).
CI runs `gen_regmap.py --check` and fails on drift.
notes: The slave claims 0x000..0xFFF (addr[15:12]==0); sally_rom_loader OR-muxes at 0x1000+.
Every register is 32-bit word-aligned (Xil_In32/Out32, no byte-lane tricks); reads never alias writes.
Runs on clk_sys (same domain as the blitter) — no CDC on the register bus.

blocks.name: BLITTER
blocks.desc: blit regs (offset = bl_addr) + STATUS/SEQ reads; dual-access 6502 $D4Bx/$D4Cx/$D4Ex under UNLK_BLIT

ranges.desc: blitter registers DST/PAT/CMD/SRC/FLAGS (bl_addr = offset); see blitter.h XT_BL_*
SRC/DST DDR-surface descriptors / ROW0 bases (bl_addr = offset)

regs.desc: {pat_blocked[2], queue_full[1], busy[0]}
seq_counter[15:0]

blocks.name: SPRITE
blocks.desc: sprite-engine reg index/data port; dual-access 6502 $D4Ax/$D4Dx under UNLK_SPRITE

regs.desc: latch sprite reg index
sprite reg data + strobe (writes idx/data to engine)
collision[col_sel] (set col_sel first via $D4D9); [15:0] = sprites this one hit
[0]=enable; also toggles the commit flag
DDR byte address (32-bit)
on-screen X (12-bit)
on-screen Y (12-bit)
width px (12-bit; stride = w<<2)
height px (12-bit)

blocks.name: CTRL
blocks.desc: control plane (gp0_ctrl, SALLY speed, XT unlock, keyboard inject)

regs.desc: [0]=bars, [3:1]=XL scale, [4]=DMACTL-blank, [5]=video-sleep (gate clk_pix off) (A9-only); read = effective
SALLY clock_mult (dual: 6502 $D4CA); read = effective. W -> bl_addr $D4CA
XT register-unlock (dual: 6502 $D1DF); read = effective
KBCODE + POKEY IRQ (A9-only; emits $D4CF)
all-keys-up (A9-only; emits $D4CD)
Atari BREAK (A9-only; emits $D4CB)

compositor plane arrangement (A9-only; reset 0x210 = current). depth: [3:0]=desktop, [7:4]=overlay, [11:8]=XL. alpha_en: [16]=desktop, [17]=overlay, [18]=XL. Route-A flip = desktop on top with alpha (0x00010132)

[0]=1 HOLD the SALLY realm in reset (A9-only; reset 0 = running). Cold-boot-per-launch: hold, rewrite the OS/RAM through the ROM-loader window (0x1000+), release = fresh coldstart. Resets the 6502 core AND the XT state a stock guest cannot know about (bank selects $D5C0/$D5C1, screen banking $D5C3-5); the video pipeline keeps scanning

keypad->joystick override (A9-only; forces STICK0/1 PORTA pins + TRIG0 when the physical PCAL9722 joystick is absent). [31]=override enable (0 = joy_bridge/PCAL9722 drives as normal). [7:0]=PORTA pin value, ACTIVE-LOW (STICK0 bits[3:0]: bit0=up bit1=down bit2=left bit3=right; STICK1 bits[7:4]; 1=released 0=pressed; 0xFF=neutral). [8]=TRIG0/fire value, ACTIVE-LOW (0=fire pressed). Muxed into pia_regs PORTA + GTIA TRIG0 in antic_top; the joy_bridge write-through path is untouched

console-keys value the 6502 reads as CONSOL ($D01F). ACTIVE-LOW: bit0=START bit1=SELECT bit2=OPTION (0=pressed). Reset $07 (none). The kernel holds OPTION ($03) across a game coldstart so the XL OS leaves BASIC DISABLED ($A000-$BFFF stays RAM) — no game boots with BASIC mapped, and BASIC shadowing RAM was crashing games; releases to $07 for boot-to-BASIC (READY). Replaces the hardwired 8'h07 in antic_top

ANTIC-rewrite timing tune (A9-only; reset 0 = the RTL defaults). Four SIGNED nibble offsets on the cycle numbers ACID bisects, so a cycle question costs a register write instead of a 25-minute bitstream: [3:0] NMIST status cycle (default 7), [7:4] /NMI cycle (8), [11:8] WSYNC /RDY release (104), [15:12] VCOUNT advance (111). The legacy timing machine has the same facility for its WSYNC release and that is how its constants were found. Only meaningful under rewrite timing authority (sallyrst[3])
MMCM locks / clk_pix-alive / frame count
production-chain counters
read-path activity
HP3 (XL) first-AR address
HP0 (desktop) first-AR address
HP2 read-probe status
HP2 read-probe last rdata
TEMP ROM-window upload diag: [31:16]=window AXI writes accepted, [15:0]=rom_we pulses emitted to sally_mem
TEMP ROM-window upload diag: [23:8]=last rom_addr, [7:0]=last rom_data

blocks.name: XLCTL
blocks.desc: XL compositor-plane window placement (A9-positioned emulation window)

regs.desc: plane origin X on screen (12-bit)
plane origin Y on screen (12-bit)
clip width  (12-bit; clip_x1 = X + W)
clip height (12-bit; clip_y1 = Y + H)
integer scale 1..5
[0]=1: use these regs (A9-positioned); 0: legacy gp0_ctrl-scale centred

blocks.name: MATH
blocks.desc: math-coprocessor mailbox (A9-only); 6502 side = $D5C6-$D5C8 + the $4000-$5FFF math page

regs.desc: doorbell event pop: [8]=valid, [7:0]=chunk index; a read consumes one event; IRQ_F2P[1] level = FIFO non-empty
completion: [7:0]=chunk, [15:8]=result-span first line (64 B lines), [23:16]=line count; reloads the span into the math page if that chunk is resident, then raises $D5C7 done
[0]=engine busy, [1]=chunk resident/ready, [2]=evt FIFO non-empty, [15:8]=resident chunk, [23:16]=evt FIFO fill

blocks.name: TRNG
blocks.desc: hardware entropy (ring-oscillator TRNG in the PL; A9-only, read-only)

regs.desc: whitened 32-bit entropy word (free-running pool snapshot); read repeatedly for fresh words. Entropy SOURCE for the OS pool, not raw crypto output

R [5:0]=debiased entropy bits accumulated since the last TRNG_RND read (saturates at 32), [8]=fresh (>=32 bits, i.e. a FULLY re-seeded word). Reading TRNG_RND CONSUMES and clears the counter. Poll bit 8 before taking key material: the pool refills ~32 bits per microsecond, far slower than back-to-back AXI reads, so un-gated reads return an LFSR-stretched pool rather than fresh entropy

blocks.name: DEBUG
blocks.desc: in-fabric 6502 debugger (xt6502_debug): halt/step/breakpoint/register access, driving /bin/6502. Halt is a non-destructive rdy-gate (state preserved); all actions align to the ST_FETCH instruction boundary. Status is coherent when halted (a halted core is static). Sel 0x9 is RESERVED for the future ANTIC debugger. See docs/OS/6502-debug.md

regs.desc: write (any) -> run to the next instruction boundary, then freeze (state preserved). Also arms halt-at-reset when combined with a SALLYRST pulse
write (any) -> release the core, run at the configured speed
write N -> execute exactly N instructions (min 1) then freeze
[0]=bkpt_en (arm the PC breakpoint), [1]=halt_at_reset (freeze at the reset-vector fetch after the next SALLYRST release)
[15:0]=breakpoint PC; when bkpt_en, the core freezes at the ST_FETCH of this address (before executing it)
write (any) -> inject DBG_WPC/WAXYS/WPSH into the core's PC/regs and re-anchor at ST_FETCH (only meaningful while halted)
[15:0]=PC to inject on DBG_COMMIT
regs to inject on DBG_COMMIT: [7:0]=A [15:8]=X [23:16]=Y [31:24]=SP(low)
inject on DBG_COMMIT: [7:0]=P (NV-BDIZC) [11:8]=SP high nibble (12-bit xt stack)
[0]=halted [1]=bkpt_hit [2]=stepping [3]=running
[15:0]=PC snapshot at the last instruction boundary (coherent when halted = next instruction to execute)
snapshot: [7:0]=P [11:8]=SP high nibble
retired-instruction count since SALLYRST (increments on each ST_FETCH boundary)

R ANTIC beam position latched when the core HALTED at an instruction boundary: [15:0]=scanline (0..261), [22:16]=beam X in ANTIC machine cycles (0..113). Lets an instruction be read off against the cycle numbers ACID annotates its kernels with; the trace ring records PC but not the beam. Reflects the REWRITE's beam (antic_gtia), whichever authority is selected
instruction-trace ring: [0]=enable (capture {PC,A,X,Y,SP,P} every ST_DECODE boundary), [1]=break_on_full (halt the core when the ring wraps). Ring is 4096 deep; readable only when halted (static).
trace write pointer: [11:0]=next write slot (newest = WPTR-1), [16]=wrapped (ring has been full at least once), [17]=broke_on_full
set the ring read index (0..4095); the entry appears in DBG_TRC_PC/AXYS/P
[15:0]=PC of the traced instruction at DBG_TRC_IDX
traced regs at DBG_TRC_IDX: [7:0]=A [15:8]=X [23:16]=Y [31:24]=SP(low)
traced at DBG_TRC_IDX: [7:0]=P [11:8]=SP high nibble
[15:0]=data watchpoint address; when armed the core freezes on a bus access to it
data watchpoint arm: [0]=enable, [1]=break on WRITE to DBG_WP, [2]=break on READ of DBG_WP (set both for any access)

debug self-observability (clk_sally, coherent when halted): [1:0]=cfg_s (CDC-synced DBG_CFG), [2]=bkpt_fire seen since arm, [3]=wp_fire seen since arm, [4]=last halt was a watchpoint, [31:16]=bkpt_s (CDC-synced DBG_BKPT — verify it matches what was written)

FIDELITY streaming-trace control: [0]=strm_en (capture {PC,A,X,Y,SP,P,IR} per instruction into a 4096-deep ring; the core AUTO-HALTS when the ring fills = real stop-the-world), [1]=drain_done (4-phase level handshake: after draining STRM_RD* set this to clear flush_req, reset the ring, and resume the core; then clear it). Rising edge of strm_en resets the ring.
[0]=flush_req: the streaming ring is FULL and the core is halted; the A9 should drain STRM_RD* (0..STRM_WPTR-1) then pulse drain_done
[12:0]=count of valid entries in the streaming ring (4096 when full; a smaller partial count if strm_en was cleared mid-window)
[11:0]=streaming ring read address; the entry appears in STRM_RDLO/RDHI (coherent while flush_req — the ring is static because the core is halted)
streaming entry [31:0] at STRM_RADDR: [15:0]=PC [23:16]=A [31:24]=X
streaming entry [63:32] at STRM_RADDR: [7:0]=Y [15:8]=SP [23:16]=P [31:24]=IR

ANTIC timebase probe config: [2:0]=mode (0=off 1=$D4xx write@match 2=$D4xx read@match 3=DLI-line 4=VBI 5=WSYNC($D40A wr) 6=any $D4xx wr 7=every line_start), [11:4]=match_addr (low byte of $D4xx reg), [19:16]=read_idx (0..15 ring entry selected into DBG_TB_CAP), [24]=clear (write with a mode to arm+reset the ring for a fresh capture), [25]=circular (0=stop-on-full: hold the FIRST 16 triggers then freeze; 1=wrap: hold the LAST 16 triggers, DBG_TB_STAT.wr_idx = oldest entry), [28:26]=WSYNC /RDY shape mask {latch,q1,q2} (0 = default = 011 q1|q2; see wsync_gen.sv; [14]=comb fallback, [15]=disable write immunity, [23:20]=signed release-cycle offset from 103). 2-FF synced into the ANTIC clk_bus domain.

ANTIC timebase probe status (2-FF synced from clk_bus): [15:0]=trig_count (16-bit saturating # of triggers since clear), [20:16]=wr_idx (0..16; 16=full), [24]=full (ring holds 16 entries), [25]=armed (set by a clear write)

ANTIC timebase probe capture: ring entry selected by DBG_TB_CFG.read_idx = {[24:16]=scanline (0..261), [15:8]=phi2_in_line (machine-cycle 0..113), [7:0]=data (write byte for write modes, ANTIC read byte for read mode, 0 for event modes)}

blocks.name: SIO
blocks.desc: paravirtual SIO mailbox (xt_sio_mbox): the 512 B page the XL OS boot stub shares with the A9, plus its data window. The doorbell/completion/status legs are the MATH block's ($D5C7 done, MATH_EVT, MATH_DONE, IRQ_F2P[1]) so the worker-task and IRQ wiring are unchanged; only the payload window is here. Sel 0x9 stays RESERVED for the ANTIC debugger. See hdl/xt_sio_mbox.sv

regs.desc: byte pointer into the 512 B mailbox (word-aligned; [1:0] ignored). Writing it re-aims the window; each SIO_DAT access then auto-increments by 4, so a run of bytes is one seek plus N accesses

32-bit little-endian word at the pointer; read or write auto-increments the pointer by 4. The BRAM read register tracks the pointer continuously and consecutive AXI transactions are tens of clocks apart, so a read always returns settled data
